# `set_page`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Switch the device to a named application page (preview, focus, autosave, pa, stack, rtmp or plan).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xd0e20, SetPage @0x129f20, get_page_id @0x146820; CamExpose @0x2189d0 (mode 2 and page 6 compares @0x219208, @0x219268) (64-bit build) |

Selects the active application page, which changes exposure mode, binning, per-page control values and stream state. The page is written to the device state even when the camera is not connected and the call then fails with 318. A success reply acknowledges the page change, not the completion of any exposure. Page ids are 0 preview, 1 focus, 2 autosave, 3 pa, 4 stack, 5 rtmp and 6 plan; the lookup returns the sentinel 7 for an unknown name, which gives 109, and a non-string params value gives 105 before any lookup. Every page other than preview, focus and pa sets exposure mode 2. For plan the handler first checks the exposure worker and returns 268 while it runs. To run a legacy plan a client enables exactly the plan to run, sends set_page plan, then start_exposure. On the exposure worker, mode 2 on the plan page runs the enabled-plan runner, and mode 2 on any other page runs the sequence list. stop_exposure stops the run.

Side effects: Changes the active page; clears delayed configuration on a change; can stop RTMP streaming or polar alignment when leaving a page; changes exposure mode and binning; calls the camera page setter; restores per-page controls; starts RTMP when entering the rtmp page.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_page"`. [READ] |
| `params` | string\|array | yes | - | The page name, as a bare string, or an array whose first element is the page name (further elements ignored; an empty array is treated as absent). There is no object form and no `page` key. Name matching is case-insensitive. Accepted names: preview, focus, autosave, pa, stack, rtmp, plan (device page ids 0 to 6 in that order). An absent, null, object, numeric, boolean or non-string first-element params value gives 105; any other string gives 109. No default. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | params absent, null, or not a string (or an array whose first element is not a string) | `expected string param` |
| 109 | Page name not one of the seven recognised names | `unexpected param` |
| 318 | Camera closed or absent; the page value may nevertheless have been written | `device not connected` |
| 268 | Target is the plan page while the exposure worker thread is running | `operation is in progress` |
| 207 | A helper failed and left error code 0 (reported as fail to operate) | `fail to operate` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Errors propagated by the exposure-mode, RTMP and binning helpers and by camera callbacks are not enumerated (unresolved); they arrive as unnamed codes from the shared table.

## Example

Request, preview - Select the preview page (shape INFERRED):

```json
{"id":21,"method":"set_page","params":"preview"}
```

Request, array-form - Array form, first element used:

```json
{"id":22,"method":"set_page","params":["focus"]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_page","result":0,"code":0,"id":21}
```

Reply, unknown-page:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_page","error":"unexpected param","code":109,"id":23}
```
